pharm: Sulfhydryl (thiol) compound that binds and detoxifies the urotoxic metabolites of oxazaphosphorines (ifosfamide/cyclophosphamide) within the urinary tract, preventing haemorrhagic cystitis
quick: 20% of the ifosfamide dose (w/w) IV at 0, 4 and 8 h; or 20% IV at 0 h then 40% orally at 2 and 6 h
Oral mesna may be taken with or without food; given on a fixed schedule relative to ifosfamide
Used with ifosfamide, which can cause fetal harm; refer to the ifosfamide information
Data lacking; defer to the cytotoxic regimen, during which breastfeeding is not advised
Patients with renal failure generally require the usual mesna dose
No specific dose adjustment described for mesna itself
Daily urinalysis for haematuria; ensure adequate hydration/urine output
summary: Mesna (sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate) is a cytoprotective thiol agent indicated as a prophylactic agent to reduce the incidence of ifosfamide-induced haemorrhagic cystitis. In the urinary tract it reacts with the urotoxic ifosfamide metabolites acrolein and 4-hydroxy-ifosfamide and detoxifies them, protecting the bladder mucosa. The total daily dose equals 60% of the ifosfamide dose, given either as three IV boluses each of 20% of the ifosfamide dose (w/w) at 0, 4 and 8 hours, or as a single IV bolus of 20% at 0 hours followed by two oral doses of 40% each at 2 and 6 hours. The schedule is repeated on each day ifosfamide is given, and the mesna-to-ifosfamide ratio is maintained if the ifosfamide dose changes. Mesna does not reduce the systemic anticancer effect of ifosfamide and is not indicated to reduce haematuria from other causes such as thrombocytopenia. Hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis) and serious dermatologic reactions can occur, and the injection's benzyl alcohol must be avoided in premature/low-birth-weight infants.
indications: Prophylaxis to reduce the incidence of ifosfamide-induced haemorrhagic cystitis
Limitation: not indicated to reduce the risk of haematuria from other causes such as thrombocytopenia

dosage.d: Mesna 240 mg/m2 (20% of an ifosfamide dose of 1.2 g/m2, w/w) IV at 0, 4 and 8 hours; total daily mesna dose 60% of the ifosfamide dose
dosage.t: IV bolus at 0, 4 and 8 hours; repeat each day ifosfamide is given
dosage.n: Maintain the mesna:ifosfamide ratio if the ifosfamide dose is changed

dosage.d: Mesna 240 mg/m2 IV (20%) at 0 hours, then mesna tablets 480 mg/m2 (40%) orally at 2 and 6 hours
dosage.t: Single IV bolus at 0 h, oral doses at 2 and 6 h; repeat each ifosfamide day
dosage.n: If a patient vomits within 2 hours of an oral dose, repeat the dose or give IV mesna

admin: Give the dosing schedule on each day that ifosfamide is administered and maintain the mesna-to-ifosfamide ratio when the ifosfamide dose is adjusted
Maintain adequate urinary output as required for ifosfamide treatment and monitor urine for haematuria
Mesna injection is for IV use; it may be given undiluted but, if dilution is desired, D5W or normal saline may be used (diluted solutions contain no preservative and should not be stored)
Avoid the benzyl-alcohol-preserved injection in premature neonates and low-birth-weight infants
Do not mix with chemotherapy in the same container unless compatibility is established
moa: Mesna is a synthetic sulfhydryl (thiol) compound. After administration it is rapidly oxidised to its inactive disulfide dimesna in the circulation; in the kidney dimesna is reduced back to the active free thiol, which is concentrated in the urinary tract. There it reacts chemically with the urotoxic ifosfamide metabolites: it binds 4-hydroxy-ifosfamide to form a non-urotoxic 4-sulfoethylthioifosfamide and binds the double bonds of acrolein and other urotoxic metabolites, neutralising their irritant effect on the bladder urothelium. Because mesna acts within the urinary tract and does not enter cells appreciably, it protects the bladder without reducing the systemic antitumour activity of ifosfamide.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to mesna or to any of the excipients, including benzyl alcohol
relative: Premature neonates and low-birth-weight infants (benzyl-alcohol-containing injection)
History of adverse reactions to other thiol compounds (e.g. amifostine)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis during/after infusion
Skin for rash, urticaria, angioedema or severe cutaneous reactions
Urine for haematuria and adequate output/hydration

preg: Mesna is used in combination with ifosfamide or other cytotoxic agents. Ifosfamide can cause fetal harm including embryo-fetal lethality, so refer to the ifosfamide prescribing information regarding use in pregnancy. The injection contains benzyl alcohol, but because benzyl alcohol is rapidly metabolised by a pregnant woman, fetal exposure is unlikely.
lact: Specific data on mesna in breast milk are lacking. As it is used as part of cytotoxic (ifosfamide-based) chemotherapy, breastfeeding is generally not recommended during the treatment regimen; follow the guidance for the accompanying chemotherapy.
renal: Patients with renal failure will generally require the usual doses of mesna; no specific reduction is described. Adequate hydration and urine output remain essential during ifosfamide therapy.
hepatic: No specific mesna dose adjustment is described for hepatic impairment.

interactions.food: Oral mesna may be taken with or without food on the scheduled timing relative to ifosfamide
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported with mesna
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive tests for urinary ketones and can interfere with enzymatic CPK (creatine phosphokinase) activity assays

common: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal pain (reactions reported when given with ifosfamide)
Leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anaemia, granulocytopenia (largely attributable to the chemotherapy regimen)
serious: Severe cutaneous reactions: drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis
Benzyl alcohol toxicity in premature/low-birth-weight infants (gasping syndrome)
emergency: Anaphylaxis with respiratory distress and circulatory collapse

monitoring: Daily urinalysis for haematuria during ifosfamide therapy
Adequate urinary output and hydration status
Observation for hypersensitivity reactions during and after administration
Skin examination for rash or severe cutaneous reaction
counsel: This medicine protects your bladder from the side effects of your chemotherapy (ifosfamide)
Drink plenty of fluids and pass urine frequently; report any blood in the urine or pain on passing urine
Tell the team straight away if you develop a rash, itching, swelling, breathing difficulty, fever or feel faint
Take each oral dose at the scheduled time; if you vomit soon after an oral dose, tell your nurse so it can be repeated
pk: Acts rapidly within the urinary tract; protective free thiol appears in urine soon after dosing
Plasma peak of free mesna is reached within about 0.5-1.5 hours after IV; oral somewhat later
Short - elimination half-life of free mesna about 0.4 hour and of total mesna about 1.2 hours
Schedule provides bladder protection across the 8-12 hours of ifosfamide metabolite exposure; doses repeated each treatment day
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); do not store diluted/preservative-free solutions
pearls: Total daily mesna dose = 60% of the ifosfamide dose, given as 20% boluses (IV) or 20% IV + 40% oral x2
Acts as a uroprotectant by detoxifying acrolein and 4-hydroxy-ifosfamide in urine without reducing antitumour effect
Maintain hydration and check urine daily for haematuria; repeat oral dose if vomited within 2 hours
Can cause false-positive urinary ketone tests and interfere with CPK assays
Watch for hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and severe skin reactions (DRESS, SJS/TEN); avoid benzyl-alcohol injection in neonates
missed: Mesna is given on a strict schedule alongside ifosfamide by the chemotherapy team. If an oral dose is vomited within 2 hours or is missed, inform the team so it can be repeated or given intravenously - skipping a dose can leave the bladder unprotected.
overdose: There is no known specific antidote. Reported effects after high doses include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever and, with very large amounts, hypersensitivity reactions with mild hypotension, dyspnoea, asthma exacerbation, rash and flushing. Management is supportive with monitoring of vital signs and treatment of hypersensitivity.
